help.detail.history.undo: Steps this layer back to how it was before the last change. Every change is kept, so you can walk back as far as you need.
help.detail.history.redo: Steps forward again after an undo.

slash.tutorial: Guided beginner tour with a beeing
tutorial.go-in: To go inside a tile, just left-click it. Watch me!
tutorial.inside: We’re in! Everything here lives inside “{cell}”. The address up here always shows where you are.
tutorial.go-out: Three ways back out: right-click anywhere, hold Shift and click, or press the Back button. I’ll use Back.
tutorial.back: And we’re back where we started. In and out — that’s the heartbeat of Hypercomb.
tutorial.create: This is the command line — the fastest way to build. Type a name and press Enter, and a tile is born. I’ll make “{name}”.
tutorial.your-tile: Meet “{name}” — a brand-new tile with a proper cover image. Anything you can name, you can make.
tutorial.children-intro: Tiles hold tiles. Let’s step inside and give it seven children — one for each day of the week.
tutorial.brackets: A power move: square brackets create many tiles at once. One line, seven days — watch!
tutorial.children-done: Monday through Sunday — seven child tiles, each with its own cover. Your world grows tile by tile, as deep as you like.
tutorial.travel: Now let’s travel between them, exactly like before: click a tile to go in, Shift+click to come back out.
tutorial.travel-done: In, out, and across — you can wander anywhere. You can’t get lost: Back and Home always know the way.
tutorial.zoom: Roll the mouse wheel to zoom in and out — pinch on a touch screen. A quick demo…
tutorial.pan: Hold the Space bar and drag to glide across the honeycomb. On a touch screen, one finger drags.
tutorial.home: And whenever you’re done exploring, the Home button brings you straight back to your front door.
tutorial.done: That’s the basics! Click to go in · right-click or Shift+click to go out · type a name to create · wheel zooms · Space drags · Home resets. Type /help whenever you want more.
tutorial.practice: First, let me open a clean practice page — nothing on your pages will change, and I’ll tidy it away when we’re done.
tutorial.cleanup: That was our practice page — watch me tidy it away. Build the real thing on any page: you know how now.
tutorial.welcome.beginner: Good — you can move and make. Now the everyday verbs: picking tiles, editing them, notes, copy, remove, and taking anything back.
tutorial.welcome.intermediate: This one is about MEANING: marks that gather tiles into collections, titles, references, and history as somewhere you can travel.
tutorial.welcome.expert: This one is the WINDOWS — one lesson per surface in front of you, and every behaviour that lives in it. By the end there is nothing on your screen you cannot name.
tutorial.done.beginner: That’s the everyday kit: Ctrl+click selects · E edits · Ctrl+C copies and Enter places · Delete removes · Ctrl+Z takes it back. Ready for more? Type /tutorial intermediate.
tutorial.done.intermediate: Marks gather, titles rename without moving, references point, history remembers. When you want the powerful stuff, type /tutorial expert.
tutorial.done.expert: That’s every primary window and what it is for. Any one of them alone: /tutorial window-tags, window-history, window-workflow… and /help opens the reference sheet, with every behaviour and shortcut in one searchable list.
tutorial.select: A plain click goes INSIDE a tile. To pick tiles without leaving, hold Ctrl and click — that selects. Ctrl+drag paints a whole run of them.
tutorial.selected: Two tiles picked. Selection is what every command acts on — copy, cut, remove, keywords. Ctrl+click a selected tile again to drop it.
tutorial.edit: Hover a tile and press E — or click its pencil — to open the editor. Words, pictures, links: the tile’s contents live there.
tutorial.editor: Type to write, drop a picture in, and Escape closes it again. Nothing is lost — every change becomes one revision you can walk back.
tutorial.note: Every tile can carry notes — the explanation that belongs WITH the thing, not in some other document. Let me leave one.
tutorial.note-done: That note now travels with the tile: share it, adopt it, walk its history — the note comes too.
tutorial.note.sample: A note lives on the tile — anyone who visits reads it here.
tutorial.note.window: Notes nest, take marks, and reorder — the reasoning lives beside the thing it is about.
tutorial.lesson.title: Rename without moving
tutorial.lesson.window-help: The reference and the docs reader
tutorial.copy: Pick a tile and press Ctrl+C. The copy carries everything — its pictures, its notes, its whole branch.
tutorial.paste: Now press Enter and it drops wherever you are standing. Watch — inside “{cell}”.
tutorial.paste-done: Same tile, second home. Cut (Ctrl+X) does the same but takes it with you instead of leaving the original.
tutorial.remove: Select a tile and press Delete. If it has anything nested inside, you get asked first — a branch never leaves quietly.
tutorial.remove-done: Gone from the page — but not from history. Nothing you do here is unrecoverable; the next lesson brings it straight back.
tutorial.undo: Ctrl+Z walks the page back one change. Every single thing you do is one revision — so undo always knows exactly what to take back.
tutorial.redo: Back it comes. Ctrl+Y steps forward again — you can walk your work in both directions.
tutorial.fit: Wandered off? Fit brings the whole page back into view in one move — the button in the bar, or its key.
tutorial.fit-done: Everything back on screen. Between Fit, Back and Home you can always get your bearings.
tutorial.arrange: Tiles fill the page in a sequence — a spiral, a line, a ring. Cycle the sequence and the page rearranges itself.
tutorial.arrange-done: Same tiles, different shape. You can also drag a tile where you want it — the arrangement is yours, and it is remembered.
tutorial.keyword: Tiles carry MARKS — pheromones. A mark says what a tile is, and anything wearing the same mark belongs together, wherever it lives.
tutorial.keyword-done: Both tiles now wear “{mark}”. Paint the same mark anywhere in your hive and those tiles join the same collection — no folder, no moving anything.
tutorial.filter: Type >? in the command line and the page filters as you type — by name, by mark, live. It never moves anything; it just narrows what you see.
tutorial.filter-done: Only what matches is left standing. /clear puts everything back — the filter is a lens, never a change.
tutorial.chip.title: Titles
tutorial.title: A tile’s NAME is its address — everything points at it. So renaming does not move it: /title gives it new words to draw under, and every link stays good.
tutorial.title-done: It reads as “{title}” now, and it is still exactly where it was. /title {cell} = clears it again.
tutorial.reference: One thing often belongs in several places. A reference tile is a live pointer: click it and you land on the real thing, which stays where it lives.
tutorial.reference-done: That new tile is a doorway, not a copy. Change the original and the doorway shows the change — one truth, many ways in.
tutorial.into: A reference lends a tile a second doorway and leaves it where it is. Filing is the other act: the tile MOVES. It goes inside another tile and stops being on this page at all.
tutorial.into-done: There they are, living in “{cell}”. The page you took them from does not hold them any more — that is what makes this tidying rather than tagging. Undo puts them straight back; nothing was deleted.
tutorial.into-organizer: Portals do this across your whole hive. Walk into a collection, pick tiles wherever they are, and it offers both verbs: Add leaves them where they live, Move brings them in. Holding Ctrl while you drag one tile onto another is the same act again, on one page.
tutorial.palette: Every action in the hive is in one list. Open the palette, start typing what you want, and it finds it — you never have to remember a shortcut.
tutorial.palette-done: That is the whole surface — commands, views, behaviours. Escape closes it. /help lays the same ground out as tiles you can study.
tutorial.history: Undo is only the doorway. Every change you have ever made is a revision you can travel to — the history panel is the road.
tutorial.history-done: Slide back through the revisions and the page shows you how it looked. Nothing is overwritten here — new work is always a new revision.
tutorial.snapshot: /snapshot freezes your WHOLE hive under a name — before a big rearrange, say. /restore <name> makes that moment the live hive again.
tutorial.snapshot-done: I am not running those now — they reach past our practice page, and that is yours to decide. Try them when you have something worth keeping.

hive.empty.title: Your hive is empty
hive.empty.body: Everything you keep here lives as a tile — notes, pictures, pages, whole projects. Name your first one, or let the bee show you around.
hive.empty.notice: Add the first thing you want to keep.
hive.empty.action.detail: Name the first thing you want to keep
hive.empty.tour.detail: Follow the bee for a one-minute tour
tutorial.go-in.touch: To go inside a tile, just tap it. Watch me!
tutorial.go-out.touch: Two ways back out: the Back button at the bottom of the screen, or swipe in from the right edge. I’ll use Back.
tutorial.create.touch: This is the command line, always waiting at the top. Type a name, tap GO, and a tile is born. I’ll make “{name}”.
tutorial.travel.touch: Now let’s travel between them, exactly like before: tap a tile to go in, Back to come out.
tutorial.zoom.touch: Pinch with two fingers to zoom in and out. A quick demo…
tutorial.pan.touch: Drag with one finger to glide across the honeycomb.
tutorial.home.touch: And whenever you’re done exploring, the address bar at the top takes you straight back to your front door.
tutorial.edit.touch: Tap a tile to open it full screen — its picture, its notes, and the buttons that act on it. The pencil there opens the editor.
tutorial.editor.touch: Type to write, drop a picture in, and the close button puts it away. Nothing is lost — every change becomes one revision you can walk back.
tutorial.done.touch: That’s the basics! Tap to go in · Back to go out · type a name to create · pinch to zoom · one finger drags. Happy building!
